root_cause.text: In the qcom camss VFE interrupt handler, vfe_isr() incorrectly used the write-master count MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM as the loop bound for calling vfe_isr_reg_update(), causing indices 4–6 to be used on the smaller vfe->line[VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX] array and triggering out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit state that vfe_isr() iterated with MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM(7) and passed that index to vfe_isr_reg_update(), while struct vfe contains `line[VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX]` with VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX(4); the patch fixes this by splitting the single loop into one bounded by `MAX_VFE_OUTPUT_LINES` for `vfe_isr_reg_update()` and a separate loop bounded by `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM` for write-master completion handling.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE and commit state that vfe_isr() iterated with MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM(7) and passed that index to vfe_isr_reg_update(), while struct vfe contains `line[VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX]` with VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX(4); the patch fixes this by splitting the single loop into one bounded by `MAX_VFE_OUTPUT_LINES` for `vfe_isr_reg_update()` and a separate loop bounded by `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM` for write-master completion handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle RDI register-update interrupts across all VFE output lines by separating them from write-master completion IRQ processing.
intent_record.what: The single loop over `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM` in `vfe_isr()` was split into two loops: a new first loop iterates from `0` to `MAX_VFE_OUTPUT_LINES` and handles `BUS_IRQ_MASK_0_RDI_RUP(vfe, i)` by calling `vfe_isr_reg_update(vfe, i)`, and the existing WM IRQ handling for `BUS_IRQ_MASK_0_COMP_DONE(vfe, RDI_COMP_GROUP(i))` with `vfe_buf_done(vfe, i)` remains in a separate second loop over `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, register-update IRQs for all VFE output lines are now processed using the correct output-line count instead of being limited to the number of image masters, while buffer-done IRQs continue to be handled only for valid write masters. This fixes missed RDI register-update handling when the number of output lines exceeds the number of image masters.

grouping_result.intent: Handle RDI register-update interrupts across all VFE output lines by separating them from write-master completion IRQ processing.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly alters how register-update interrupts are iterated and handled across VFE output lines instead of using write-master-based processing, which addresses the root cause of using the wrong loop bound and indexing past the smaller vfe->line array.

candidates.rationale: This loop uses MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM as the bound while also invoking vfe_isr_reg_update(vfe, i). Since vfe_isr_reg_update indexes vfe->line with i, iterating past VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX causes out-of-bounds access for indices 4-6.

This call is vulnerable because it receives i from a loop bounded by MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM rather than the size of vfe->line, directly triggering out-of-bounds indexing inside vfe_isr_reg_update for higher i values.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop uses MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM as the iteration bound while the loop index is later passed to vfe_isr_reg_update(), which indexes the smaller vfe->line array. That allows indices beyond VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX and causes the out-of-bounds access.
This call consumes the loop index i derived from the incorrect MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM bound, directly triggering out-of-bounds indexing inside vfe_isr_reg_update() for indices 4 through 6.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant interrupt handler logic directly, so it is sufficient to decide. In `vfe_isr()`, the new code changes single-line handling into a loop: `for (i = 0; i < MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM; i++) { ... vfe_isr_reg_update(vfe, i); ... vfe_isr_wm_done(vfe, i); }`. The root cause states the bug is using `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM` as the loop bound when calling `vfe_isr_reg_update()`, because that allows indices 4-6 to be used on the smaller `vfe->line[...]` array. This vulnerable construct is present exactly here. The same commit also introduces `#define MAX_VFE_OUTPUT_LINES 4` and sets `vfe->line_num = MAX_VFE_OUTPUT_LINES;`, confirming the line array is intended for 4 output lines, while the ISR loop iterates up to `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM`, not the line count. There is no fix in this function to limit the loop to the valid line range before calling `vfe_isr_reg_update()`. Therefore the bug is present and not fixed.
